subject: How to modify the font of all text in a plot.

messages.author: a1331fc093f52833
messages.subject: How to modify the font of all text in a plot.
parts:
Hi ggplot2ers,

I am trying to change the fonts of all the texts in a graph. I have
been trying the following:

######################
fontsize <- 12
old_theme <-
theme_update(axis.text.x=theme_text(size=fontsize),axis.text.y=theme_text(size=fontsize),

axis.title.x=theme_text(size=fontsize),axis.title.y=theme_text(size=fontsize),

strip.text.x=theme_text(size=fontsize),strip.text.y=theme_text(size=fontsize),

legend.text=theme_text(size=fontsize),legend.title=theme_text(size=fontsize))

n <- 100; x1 <- cbind(1:n,rnorm(n,sd=10)); x2 <-
cbind(1:n,rnorm(n,sd=3))
df <- data.frame(rbind(x1,x2)); names(df) <- c("x","y_variable"); df
$metric<-as.factor(c(rep("A",n),rep("B",n)));
bi <- ggplot(df, aes(x=x)) + geom_line(aes(y=y_variable)) +
facet_wrap(~metric,nrow=1,ncol=2); print(bi)
######################

But this is really cumbersome. Is there an easier way of doing this?
Also, this creates two problems:
a. the labels on the axes are now too close to the axes.
b. the y.axis label is now horizontal, which is not something that I
intended to do.

Thanks a million,
Cedric

>
> n  <- 100; x1 <- cbind(1:n,rnorm(n,sd=10)); x2 <-
> cbind(1:n,rnorm(n,sd=3))
> df <- data.frame(rbind(x1,x2)); names(df) <- c("x","y_variable"); df
> $metric<-as.factor(c(rep("A",n),rep("B",n)));
> bi <-  ggplot(df, aes(x=x)) + geom_line(aes(y=y_variable)) +
> facet_wrap(~metric,nrow=1,ncol=2); print(bi)
> ######################
>
> But this is really cumbersome. Is there an easier way of doing this?
> Also, this creates two problems:
> a. the labels on the axes are now too close to the axes.
> b. the y.axis label is now horizontal, which is not something that I
> intended to do.
>
> Thanks a million,
> Cedric

Both theme_gray() and theme_bw() (the two built-in themes) have a
base_size argument that will scale all the text (and spacing)
appropriately.

bi + theme_gray(base_size = 18)

If you need to do something even more complicated, use the source of
theme_gray() or theme_bw() as a start, or at least to see everything
that needs to be adjusted for a different size.

--Brian Diggs
